title: Acceptance clause 'strands re-thicken' on QoS apply has no automated or capture-level pin (alloc→view rebuild unasserted)
evidence:
spec-e2-flow-qos.md:81: '- Given a pipe is clicked, when the QoS panel changes the lane ladder, then only that pipe's allocation changes (command into sim), strands re-thicken, and the sim hash matches an isolated sim fed the same commands.'
test_view_interaction.gd:210-214 (the only strand assertions): '	var s0 := arc.strand_point(0, 0.5)
	var s1 := arc.strand_point(1, 0.5)
	var s2 := arc.strand_point(2, 0.5)
	check(s0.distance_to(s1) > 0.05 and s1.distance_to(s2) > 0.05 and s0.distance_to(s2) > 0.05,
		"strands: the three lane points occupy distinct ring positions")'
scripts/flow_view.gd:51-52: '		elif meta.get("alloc", []) != p.alloc:
			_rebuild_view(id, p)'
scripts/pipe_arc.gd:85-89: 'func _strand_thickness(lane: int) -> float:
	# share 100% -> 1.0; share 0% -> a hairline strand (the cable still reads
	# as three strands even when a lane is unallocated)
	var share := float(_shares[lane]) / 100.0
	return share if share > 0.0 else HAIRLINE_FRAC'
detail: Two of the three acceptance claims for QoS apply are pinned (command-bus mutation + hash identity in test_view_purity), but the visible strand re-thickening is asserted nowhere: no test touches _shares/_strand_thickness or checks the view rebuilt after set_lanes; grep shows the only arc assertion is test_world.gd:134 '_radius_scale > 1.0'. Capture 07 re-applies the same 3-lane ladder idempotently, so no visual transition evidence exists either.
recommended_fix: Extend _panel_logic or _strand_geometry: apply set_lanes [50,30,20] through main._on_qos_apply, run flow_view.sync(), then check arc._shares == [50,30,20] and that an unallocated lane renders hairline (thickness 0.3) vs share-scaled.

evidence:

scripts/flow_view.gd:142-143: '			if endpoint == 1:

detail: The rebind pin covers slot-material reuse only. The cap branch (>48 in flight), the hide-unused-slots pass (the 'never ghost' guard — never asserted false after drain), and the endpoint-1 t-reversal (b→a dots render correctly) execute in tests without any assertion.

title: QosPanel guard paths are happy-path-only: open() on unknown pipe and _on_apply() after close are never exercised
evidence:
scripts/qos_panel.gd:116-118: '	var p: Dictionary = sim.pipes.get(pipe_id)
	if p == null:
		close_panel()
		return'
scripts/qos_panel.gd:166-167: 'func _on_apply() -> void:
	if _pipe_id < 0:
		return'
test_view_interaction.gd:141-147 covers only the happy path: '	panel.open(pipe_id, sim)
...
	panel._on_apply()' — grep of tests/ shows no open() call with an invalid pipe id and no _on_apply after close_panel.
detail: The panel's own error handling is implied (stale selection, closed panel) but untested: a regression that re-shows the panel on unknown pipe, or emits an apply for pipe -1, would stay green. Sim-side rejection is tested, panel-side guards are not.
recommended_fix: Two checks in _panel_logic: panel.open(9999, sim) leaves panel invisible with _pipe_id == -1; close_panel() then _on_apply() emits no apply_requested.

title: CMDS_CAP=512 command-log windowing never tested: no scenario exceeds 24 commands, so pop_front/dump divergence is unexercised
evidence:
scripts/sim/sim_core.gd:103-104: '	if command_log.size() > CMDS_CAP:
		command_log.pop_front() # newest window kept; total stays in the dump'
test_sim_flow.gd:45-46: '	check(int(sim.command_log.size()) == int(sim.commands_total) and int(sim.commands_total) == 9,
		"rejected commands are still RECORDED (deterministic audit trail): %d/%d" % [sim.command_log.size(), sim.commands_total])' — largest streams in the suite are REPLAY_CMDS (17) and view_purity (10).
detail: The capped-window state transition (log size diverging from commands_total, serialized as 'C|total|size' in dump_state) never executes in any test; a windowing bug (off-by-one, wrong order) would only surface in long replays.
recommended_fix: Add a replay-leg: apply 520+ add_pipe/set_lanes commands to two fresh sims, then check command_log.size() == 512, commands_total preserved, and both sims' dump_state byte-identical.

title: Runner's check-count gate is opt-in: a test file omitting EXPECTED_CHECKS silently loses phantom-check protection
evidence:
tests/run_tests.gd:52-55: '		var pinned: Variant = inst.get("EXPECTED_CHECKS")
		var expected: int = int(pinned) if pinned != null else -1
		if expected >= 0 and ran_checks != expected:
			printerr("  FAIL %s — check-count gate: ran %d, expected %d (checks are being eaten)" % [path, ran_checks, expected])'
test_base.gd:11-13: '## Each test file pins its own `const EXPECTED_CHECKS := N` — the runner
## fails any shortfall. Friction on purpose: a mid-script abort silently
## eating checks is exactly how the r2 phantom-check bug stayed green.'
detail: The r2 B2 anti-phantom-check gate only bites when the const exists; a future test file without EXPECTED_CHECKS passes with expected=-1 and no failure. All 12 current files pin it, but nothing enforces that for new files.
recommended_fix: Invert the gate: fail any wired test file whose EXPECTED_CHECKS is missing (expected == -1 → FAIL 'pin missing'), keeping the count equality check as-is.
